card.name: Lung and liver terms in warnings
card.fires_on: The word 'monary' in 'Pulmonary Vascular Precipitates', the open parenthesis after 'carbon monoxide' before DLCO, and 'atic' in 'hepatic'. These are in warnings and adverse reaction text about lungs and liver.

modes.label: Pulmonary embolism heading
modes.description: The second half of 'Pulmonary' in the warning heading about vascular precipitates.
modes.example: 5.2 Pulmonary Embolism due to Pul<<monary>> Vascular Precipitates Pulmonary vascular

modes.label: Parenthesis before DLCO
modes.description: The open bracket after 'carbon monoxide' that introduces the abbreviation DLCO.
modes.example: Dose-dependent reductions in forced expiratory volume over 1 second (FEV 1 ) and reductions in diffusion lung capacity for carbon monoxide<< (>>DL CO ) were observed in PON

modes.label: Hepatic
modes.description: The ending of 'hepatic' before fibrosis or cirrhosis.
modes.example: Increased nevirapine trough concentrations have been observed in some patients with hep<<atic>> fibrosis or cirrhosis.
